title: A practical guide to deep-learning light-field microscopy for 3D imaging of biological dynamics
protocol: Mount a water immersion objective on the microscope to collect epifluorescence signals from samples.
Place a mirror to reflect upright detected light from the microscope.
Position a pair of 1:1 relay lenses to relay the reflected light.
Build another pair of 1:1 relay lenses and camera before inserting the microlens array to relay the image.
Relay the NIP onto the camera sensor plane in steps 3–5.
Insert the MLA at the NIP in steps 6 and 7.
Move the RL3 to relay the back focal plane of the MLA on camera sensor plane in steps 8 and 9.
Focus the image via twisting the focus ring of the microscope until the image in the ocular is as sharp as possible.
Adjust the camera along the optical axis until the image in the camera is as clear as in the ocular.
Insert the MLA at the relayed NIP after the first pair of relay lens RL1 and RL2 to double check the precise positioning of MLA.
Choose the light field PSF calculated in step 12.
Crop 'Substacks' and light-field projection into training pairs.
Click 'Crop Test'.
The sum value and variance of each cropped block from several sub-stacks will be displayed in command window of MATLAB.
These blocks will be saved at './Data/Training Pair/WF'.
Check these saved images.
Set the parameters in Section C and click ‘Crop’.
Those cropped patches will be saved in a folder (‘./Data/TrainingPair’).
Make sure depth of the patches match the ‘StackDepth’ in step a or you choose to discard some slices when it’s less than ‘StackDepth’.
Check the training dataset of VCD network.
Set VCD model parameters.
Open ‘config.py’ included in ‘./vcdnet’.
Set the basic information of training datasets and network parameters.
Train VCD model.
Run ‘train.py’ to start model training.
Activate vcd-net environment.
Run python train.py.
Check console panel for loss values.
Determine if model optimization is proper.
Open './sample/{label}' folder.
Compare reconstruction stacks with ground truths.
Adjust data processing function in 'config.py' if needed.
Modify hyper-parameters in 'config.py' if necessary.
Change model structure parameters in 'config.py'.
Enhance fitting ability of the model.
Continue training to further converge loss.
Image freely moving C.elegans using the light-field microscope.
Load the awake L4-stage worms into a microfluidic chamber.
Mount the microfluidic chamber on the stage installed on the microscope.
Move the sample stage of the microscope to make the microfluidic chamber positioned within the center of the FOV.
Adjust the focus ring of the microscope before imaging to focus the imaging plane at the desirable plane which is typically the center plane of the whole sample.
Record calcium signals and RFP signals simultaneously at a volume rate of 100 Hz using the dual-channel light-field path.
Anesthetize zebrafish larvae with approximately 100 μL tricaine (3-aminobenzoic acid ethyl ester, 0.1 mg/mL).
Mount the fish on a cover glass using 1% low-melting agarose.
Dilute the agarose with 0.1 mg/mL tricaine to prevent zebrafish larvae revival.
Move the sample on the microscope's sample stage to position signals of interest within the field of view.
Focus the microscope at the center of the heart by twisting the focus ring before cardiac imaging.
Record light-field videos of RBCs and myocytes nuclei or myocardium in the beating zebrafish heart.
Set the exposure time to 5 ms for high-speed volumetric imaging at 200 Hz.
Acquire frames of size 768 × 768 that correspond to a lateral FOV of around 250 × 250 μm², covering 4–5 cardiac cycles.
Preprocess experimental data.
Get rectification parameters for subsequent light-field image calibration using LFDisplay software.
Open the ‘Image rectification’ section in light field 3D reconstruction software package and input the text file from step a.
Click ‘Run Rectification’ and the results will be saved at ‘./Data/02_Rectified’.
Subtract average background value in the rectified light-field image.
Load trained model and implement network inference.
Change LF2D_path in ‘config.py’ to the location of the light-field images.
Set Saving_path in ‘config.py’ for reconstructed stacks.
Run python eval.py in Anaconda command prompt.
Reconstruction results will be saved in 'Saving_path' or default folder './results'.
Install ImageJ plugin from VCD-Net package for inference stage convenience.
Ensure label in ‘config.py’ matches trained model’s name during inference.
Quantitatively analyze neuronal activity and behavior of moving C.elegans.
Map calcium dynamics based on the reconstructed results of VCD-Net.
Perform semi-automated tracking of the intensity fluctuation of each individual neuron using TrackMate Fiji Plugin.
Average all the pixels within the ROI of the neurons detected to generate the signal intensity of the neurons.
Calculate the real calcium dynamics by measuring (F-F0)/F0.
Highlight weak worm outline by implementing histogram equalization towards the MIPs of the reconstructed volumes.
Use a standard U-Net to automatically segment the shape of the worm body.
Annotate the worm body to build a training dataset.
Use a Canny filter to compute the edge of the worm body based on segmented images.
Calculate the Euclidean distance transform inside the worm body from the edge image.
Identify the ridge of the distance transformation as the center line of the worm.
Calculate changing curvatures and motion velocities of the worm based on segmented center lines at different times.
Quantitatively analyze the velocity map of RBCs in the beating zebrafish heart.
Track and calculate the velocity map of RBCs flowing in the beating zebrafish heart using Imaris (v 9.0.1, Bitplane) or TrackMate Fiji Plugin.
Calculate the velocity of identified RBCs and visualize it with Mayavi.
Analyze the volume-based ejection fraction of myocardium during heartbeat.
Segment the volume of the reconstructed myocardium using Amira.
